pr_title: Adding support for filtering pit requests by index and shard
pr_body:
This makes it so that you can have a PIT query only search given indices and shards, bringing it to parity with what scrolls support.
I'm marking this as draft because I'm not familiar with this code, and not sure if the search team even wants this feature.
Closes #85703
Relates https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-hadoop/issues/1925
pr_comments: This PR is currently failing to pass all tests because data streams don't work the way I've done it. Adding data stream support to the REST path seems straightforward enough, but EQL is using a different path than I've been testing with (TransportOpenPointInTimeAction), and that seems a lot harder to fix.

This PR works well for testing es-hadoop use of PITs, but I'm going to close it because it's not really close to ready. Here's my known to do list (there might be more)

1. Properly support datastreams (as opposed to the hack I did in TransportSearchAction).
2. Add support for all `preference` values (currently only supports `_shards`).
3. Fix all the tests that are currently braking.

issue_context.title: Support specifying index and shard in point in time request
issue_context.body:
### Description

While looking into replacing scrolls with PITs in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-hadoop/issues/1925, I noticed that PITs are missing two features that scrolls have: (1) the ability to ask for results only in certain indices and (2) the ability to ask for results only in certain shards. I'm not sure if this is needed for many other use cases, but it is critical for es-hadoop/es-spark because we create one task per shard.
I think this is pretty straightforward to do, and I'll open a draft PR for it.
comments:
Transform uses PIT but currently the PIT context holds many indices that aren't needed.

> the ability to ask for results only in certain indices and (2) the ability to ask for results only in certain shards

For the transform use case it would be good to add a query when opening the PIT. The query would figure out which shards are needed using `can_match`. The important part of the query is usually a range query.

I know you ask for feature parity with _scroll_, however it make sense to think on a higher level.

(I wonder about "certain indices", as you specify the indices when opening the pit, this is already possible)

We can get around the index limitation if we need to -- it's just a convenience to open one PIT for multiple indices. Is it cheaper performance-wise to open 100 PITs for 100 indices vs opening 1 PIT for 100 indices?
Not being able to specify which shard we want to query is a showstopper for the hadoop/spark use case though.

> For the transform use case it would be good to add a query when opening the PIT. The query would figure out which shards are needed using can_match. The important part of the query is usually a range query.

That does sound useful. But the use case with es-hadoop is that we're typically pulling out a _lot_ of data, so we wind up with a process (a mapreduce map task attempt or a spark task) getting assigned a slice of a single shard, and that's all it is supposed to read. So we might have thousands of processes at once, each reading just its part of its shard. Narrowing down the shards ahead of time would be great for performance. But since we can't be guaranteed that that will narrow it down to an amount of data a single process can handle (otherwise, why would you be using hadoop or spark?), we still need to be able to tell a task which shard to read from, which we can't do currently.
I think that this was done as part of https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/94534

review_comments: We don't want to merge this. This is just to get everything working with data streams.
